title: Most buses first, then the cheapest such fleet

blocks.text: A transit agency replaces old buses within a capital budget. The board's rule: replace as many buses as the budget allows, and among the plans that replace that many, spend the least. Many plans replace the most buses, so a single solve could return any of them; the board wants the same answer every time.
Write the model first. With $`B`$ the buses, $`c_b`$ the cost of bus $`b`$ and $`K`$ the budget, pass 1 is
\max \sum_{b \in B} x_b \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{b \in B} c_b\, x_b \le K \;\; \text{(budget)}, \qquad x_b \in \{0, 1\}

Write pass 2 in the same notation: its objective, and the row it adds (with a label) so that it cannot give up any of pass 1's buses. Then write `replacement_plan(costs, budget)`: build the model with MathOpt, solve both passes with HiGHS, and return the chosen ids in sorted order. Costs are whole numbers, so a count can be held exactly.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

EXACT = mathopt.SolveParameters(relative_gap_tolerance=0.0)


def replacement_plan(costs: dict[str, int], budget: int) -> list[str]:
    """The cheapest of the plans that replace the most buses within the budget, as sorted ids."""
    model = mathopt.Model(name="buses")
    x = {b: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{b}") for b in sorted(costs)}
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(costs[b] * x[b] for b in x) <= budget, name="budget")
    model.maximize(sum(x.values()))
    most = round(mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=EXACT).objective_value())
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(x.values()) >= most, name="keep_count")
    model.minimize(sum(costs[b] * x[b] for b in x))
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=EXACT)
    return sorted(b for b in x if result.variable_values(x[b]) > 0.5)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(replacement_plan({"B1": 300, "B2": 250, "B3": 420, "B4": 260}, 820))
